issues.description: The solution implementation of ray_sphere_intersect has its parameter order swapped compared to the function declaration in the header (and compared to the template implementation). The header (and template) declare: (const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius) but the solution's .cpp defines the function as (const float *dir, const float *origin, const float *center, const float radius). This mismatch is a structural inconsistency that will cause a linker/compile-time mismatch (or at least confusion) and leads to incorrect local variable mapping (e.g. the implementation assigns const float *o = origin; const float *u = dir; but with swapped parameters those point to different arguments). Students comparing template and solution (or building the solution) will be blocked or confused by this discrepancy.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the function definition in solution_repository/example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.cpp match the header (and the template) parameter order: use (const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius). Update local variable usage accordingly (e.g. const float *o = origin; const float *u = dir;). Alternatively, if the swapped order was intentional, update the header (and template) to match and document the change — but the simplest fix is to restore the parameter order in the .cpp to match the header and template so the code compiles and behaves as expected.

issues.description: The ray_sphere_intersect function's parameter identifiers are inconsistent between the header/template and the solution implementation. The header (and the template .cpp) declare the parameters as (origin, dir, center, radius), but the solution implementation's definition names the first two parameters as (dir, origin, center, radius). This swaps the parameter identifier names across artifacts and makes it harder for students to map the documented API (header/template) to the solution implementation: a student reading the header or the template test will expect the first argument to be 'origin' and the second to be 'dir', while the solution .cpp uses the reversed names, creating unnecessary cognitive load and potential confusion when tracing the code.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the parameter identifiers consistent across header, template and implementation. For example, change the solution implementation signature to: bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius) { ... } (and keep the existing local uses). Alternatively, update the header to match the implementation, but the least disruptive fix is to align the .cpp definition with the header/template naming so students can directly map 'origin' and 'dir' between declaration and implementation.
